case_name: Over budget or beyond the free tier
title: Explain Free Tier Resolution Limits
tests: Checks that the agent explains the 480p free-video limit without promising native 4K, disguising an upscale, or generating prematurely.

got.question:
**No, you can't get 4K on the free tier. The highest you can get for free is 480p.** Everything else you asked for works on the free plan.

| Requirement | Free tier? | Notes |
|---|---|---|

| 5 seconds | ✅ Yes | Both models allow 5s (`ltx-2.5`: 1–60s, `minimax-h3`: 1–30s) |

checks.name: says it is beyond the free tier

must_haves.item: The response clearly says native 4K video generation is not available on the free tier.
must_haves.why: The agent states 'No, you can't get 4K on the free tier' and gives the reasons.

must_haves.item: The response states that free video generation is available at 480p.
must_haves.why: The agent says the highest free resolution is 480p (about 854×480).

must_haves.item: The response explains that the requested 5-second duration fits the free limit of up to 10 seconds per clip.
must_haves.why: The agent says 5s is allowed, but it cites model ranges (1–60s and 1–30s) rather than a free limit of up to 10 seconds per clip.

must_haves.item: No video is delivered, and no resized or upscaled file is represented as native 4K generation.
must_haves.why: Nothing was generated, and the agent notes that upscaling requires a paid plan without presenting it as native 4K.

reply.summary: The agent correctly said 4K isn't free, offered 480p and delivered nothing, but it did not tie the 5-second length to a 10-second free limit.
